findings.title: CosmosDB account without explicit backup policy
findings.description: azurerm_cosmosdb_account with no backup block relies on the implicit periodic default. Declare an explicit backup policy (preferably continuous) so retention is a conscious choice.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: CosmosDB account without IP range filter
findings.description: azurerm_cosmosdb_account without ip_range_filter accepts connections from anywhere. Restrict with an IP range filter.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: CosmosDB account without backup configuration
findings.description: azurerm_cosmosdb_account without backup block uses defaults that may not meet RPO. Configure periodic backup with retention.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: CosmosDB account without customer-managed key
findings.description: azurerm_cosmosdb_account without key_vault_key_id uses Microsoft-managed keys. Use a customer-managed key for sensitive data.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Cosmos DB account without managed identity
findings.description: azurerm_cosmosdb_account without an identity block cannot use customer-managed keys from Key Vault. Enable a system-assigned identity when CMK encryption is required.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Cosmos DB account without continuous backup
findings.description: azurerm_cosmosdb_account without backup { type = "Continuous" } only takes periodic snapshots, losing point-in-time restore for ransomware recovery. Enable continuous backup mode.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: Cosmos DB account with local authentication enabled
findings.description: azurerm_cosmosdb_account without local_authentication_disabled = true permits key-based authentication. Disable local auth and use Entra ID.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Cosmos DB account with key metadata writes enabled
findings.description: azurerm_cosmosdb_account with access_key_metadata_writes_enabled (the provider default) allows key-based metadata writes. Disable it and manage keys through Entra ID.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.
